rules.rule: Declare the property class of every screw and nut; do not design to 12.9 strength when commodity 8.8 / A2-70 will be bought
rules.criterion: each fastener SKU carries a class; preload and ratings use that class (Bossard, mu 0.14, max: M5 8.8 7.0 kN, 10.9 10.3 kN, 12.9 12.0 kN; M3 8.8 2436 N, 12.9 4111 N): the catalogue's 12.9 proof loads overstate a commodity 8.8 or A2-70 screw by 40 % or more
rules.severity: warning: catalogue proof loads are class 12.9 while the SKU names no class
rules.auto: catalogue field; compare required preload with the class

rules.rule: Size the screw to the joint: preload must exceed the working load with margin; prefer a longer clamp length
rules.criterion: 0.75 x proof x n >= 2 x separating load; material under the head 1 to 3 d thick and bolt spacing 3 to 5 d (Slocum); self-loosening moment about preload x pitch / 2 (NASA-STD-5020B)
rules.severity: info: few printer joints are strength-limited
rules.where: AGENT.md: 'Bolt preload and contact' not checked
rules.auto: joint force from FEA reactions / load cases against n x preload
rules.correction: clamped length >= 3 d where vibration matters (recalled) -> material under the head 1 to 3 d (Slocum 9-10)

rules.rule: Minimum thread engagement by tapped material
rules.criterion: Bossard (coarse thread, 8.8 / 10.9 / 12.9): S235 steel 1.0 / 1.25 / 1.4 d; grey iron GJL 250 1.0 / 1.25 / 1.4 d; AlMgSi1 F32 (Rm > 330) 1.4 / 1.6 d / not tabulated; AlMg3 F18 (Rm > 180) 2 d (VDI formula 3 d); standard nut = full strength. Proposed checks: 6061 / 6082 (Rm about 290 to 310, just under F32's 330): ERROR below 1.5 d, WARNING 1.5 to 2 d on load-bearing or frequently removed joints and for 10.9 / 12.9 screws (no Bossard row for 12.9 in aluminium); soft aluminium (6063 extrusion, cast plate MIC-6 / ATP-5, 5052): ERROR below 2 d; plastic: 2 d or an insert; a catalogue part's own tapped hole follows its maker
rules.applies: screws into tapped holes; T-nuts and catalogue tapped holes exempt
rules.where: interference: thread_engagement, thread_bottoms_out (1 d steel, 1.5 d aluminium, 2 d plastic)
rules.auto: already; consider 2 d for aluminium and 1.5 d for brass
rules.note: Bossard's trials cover M6 to M16 (6g / 6H); not validated for M2.5 to M5 (MISSING.txt 5). Slocum: engagement of 1 d already matches bolt tensile strength in a same-strength section. SOURCES DISAGREE: Nord-Lock 2 d and Tameson 2 to 2.5 d for 'aluminium' (snippets) vs Bossard 1.4 d for strong Al and 2 d for soft Al. The extrusion alloy of the 2020 profile is not in the repo's vendor record.
rules.correction: aluminium 2.0 d (Nord-Lock snippet; mechloop 1.5 d) -> by alloy strength per Bossard: 6061/6082 error < 1.5 d, warning 1.5 to 2 d; soft Al (6063, MIC-6, 5052) error < 2 d

rules.rule: Do not thread deeper than the thread can use
rules.criterion: engagement <= 3 d

rules.rule: Blind tapped holes need run-out below the thread; the screw must not bottom
rules.criterion: unthreaded depth >= 1.5 d below the last full thread (taps under M6); screw tip >= 1 pitch short of the bottom
rules.severity: error if the screw bottoms (no clamp), warning for run-out

rules.rule: Use a threaded insert or a nut where a soft material is assembled repeatedly
rules.criterion: plastic or soft aluminium + a screw that is removed in service (wear part, cover) => insert or through-bolt with nut
rules.auto: threads_into plastic and screw on a declared service item

rules.rule: Clearance holes to ISO 273; choose the class deliberately
rules.criterion: ISO 273 fine / medium / coarse: M2.5 2.7/2.9/3.1, M3 3.2/3.4/3.6, M4 4.3/4.5/4.8, M5 5.3/5.5/5.8, M6 6.4/6.6/7, M8 8.4/9/10 (H12 / H13 / H14); Bossard's torque and pressure tables assume medium; larger than coarse => washer (FST-031); chamfer the hole edge under the head (MMCC note)
rules.severity: info (class), warning (under fine, or over coarse without a washer)
rules.where: tolerance: pattern start (p_all_start); parts.clearance_hole() gives one 'close' value, unverified
rules.auto: measure each hole around each screw (tools/practice_audit.py does)
rules.correction: table values recalled -> confirmed unchanged from the MMCC ISO 273 table (read from the scan)

rules.rule: Keep the pressure under the head and the nut below what the clamped material can carry
rules.criterion: p = FM max / Ap <= pG. pG (VDI 2230:2015, short-term, room temperature): S235 mild steel 490 MPa (1986 table: St 37 260), stainless X5CrNiMo 630, AW-6082 T6 (Rm 290) 360 -> used for 6061-T6 (mapped), AW-5083 325, cast GK-AlSi9Cu3 (Rm 160) 200 -> used for MIC-6 cast plate (mapped, derived), 70 % of pG where no indentation is permitted; power screwdriver up to -25 %, chamfered hole up to +25 % (steels). FM max from Bossard at mu 0.14 for the declared class (8.8 assumed when none: M3 2436 N, M5 7.0 kN)
rules.auto: preload from class torque, area from head and measured hole
rules.note: SOURCES DISAGREE: VDI 2230 1986 (St 37 260) vs 2015 (S235 490): both recorded, 2015 used. MIC-6 and 6061 are not in the table: the mapping to the nearest alloy by tensile strength is ours, labelled derived.
rules.correction: limit = yield of the clamped part (6061 276, MIC-6 105, steel 250); preload = recalled torque / (0.2 d) (M3 2167 N, M5 5700 N) -> limit = VDI 2230:2015 pG (6061 360 mapped, MIC-6 200 mapped, mild steel 490); preload = Bossard FM max, 8.8, mu 0.14 (M3 2436 N, M5 7000 N)

rules.rule: Plain washer under any head or nut that sits on a slot, an oversize hole, a soft or painted surface
rules.criterion: slot or hole larger than ISO 273 coarse, or head face supported < 80 % => washer. ISO 7089 (ID min / OD max / t): M3 3.2 / 7 / 0.5, M4 4.3 / 9 / 0.8, M5 5.3 / 10 / 1.0; ISO 7093 large: M3 3.2 / 9 / 0.8, M4 4.3 / 12 / 1.0, M5 5.3 / 15 / 1.2; ISO 7090 starts at M5, ISO 7093-1 at M3
rules.applies: slots, oversize holes, printed and thin parts
rules.severity: warning: head digs in, adjustment creeps, joint loosens
rules.auto: supported fraction of the head annulus on the first clamped part
rules.correction: ISO 7089 dims from FreeCAD CSV; ISO 7093 not fetched -> ISO 7089 confirmed (RC); ISO 7093 added (M3 9 mm, M5 15 mm OD)

rules.rule: Washer under the element that is turned on aluminium (anodised or bare) and on coated parts
rules.criterion: nut or head rotated against aluminium / paint => washer, to keep friction repeatable and the coating intact
rules.auto: material of the bearing part + which end is turned (the one with tool access)

rules.rule: Countersinks only in sheet thick enough to keep a cylindrical land
rules.criterion: sheet >= 3.18 mm for a countersink (SendCutSend); head height <= 60 % of t (recalled)

rules.rule: Leave enough floor under a counterbored head
rules.criterion: material under a head (counterbore floor, thin flange) typically 1 to 3 d thick (Slocum); below 1 d check FST-030 on the floor
rules.where: manufacture: cnc floor / wall minimums (0.5-0.8 mm only)
rules.auto: thickness of the first clamped interval when the head is recessed
rules.correction: floor >= 0.6 d (recalled) -> >= 1 d (Slocum, 'typically')

rules.rule: State a tightening torque for every structural joint; derive it from class, friction and the weakest clamped material
rules.criterion: torque from Bossard (VDI 2230:2015, 90 % of yield, max, no safety factor) at mu 0.14 (zinc-plated, the lower end of 0.14 to 0.24): class 8.8 M2.5 0.81, M3 1.41, M4 3.3, M5 6.5 N.m; 12.9 M3 2.37, M5 11.2 N.m; at mu 0.10: M3 8.8 1.12, M5 8.8 5.2 N.m; minimum preload = FM max / alphaA, alphaA 1.6 to 2.0 for a hand torque wrench; reduce to the FST-030 / PRT-030 limit on soft parts; rail bolts per Hiwin (M3 0.98 N.m in aluminium)
rules.auto: generate a torque table per screw group into BUILD.md
rules.correction: 8.8 torques M2.5 0.7, M3 1.3, M4 2.9, M5 5.7 N.m (recalled, mu about 0.14) -> M2.5 0.81, M3 1.41, M4 3.3, M5 6.5 N.m (Bossard mu 0.14); preload taken directly from the table, not from T / 0.2 d
rules.note: Friction: the screws' finish is not declared (black-oxide socket screws are not in the Bossard example); 0.14 is used as the lowest practical value Bossard tells the user to assume. SEW (snippet) uses 0.09 for 10.9 / 12.9.

rules.rule: Do not design a joint that only works at an exact preload
rules.criterion: hand torque scatter +/-35 % (feel), +/-25 % (torque wrench): a joint must work between 0.65 and 1.35 of nominal preload
rules.auto: could bracket friction-joint checks (STR-014) with 0.65x preload

rules.rule: Edge distance and pitch of fastener holes
rules.criterion: hole centre to edge: nominal 2 d, minimum 1.5 d (NASA RP-1228); Bossard's recommended minimum edge distance c: M4 6, M5 7.5 mm (= 1.5 d); pitch 4 d nominal (NASA), 3 to 5 d (Slocum)
rules.applies: metal parts; plastics want more (>= 2 d, recalled)
rules.where: manufacture: sheet.hole_to_edge_t_ratio (1 t of web: a cutting rule, not a strength rule), fdm.thread_wall_d_ratio
rules.auto: distance from each screw axis to the nearest boundary of each clamped part

rules.rule: A joint needs two fasteners, or one fastener plus a feature that stops rotation
rules.criterion: parts joined by one screw also share a pin, key, shoulder, rib-in-slot or a second screw: 'To resist rotation, a moment, or two forces acting as a couple, is required' (Slocum); one screw is one force on a line
rules.severity: warning: the part swings on its screw under vibration
rules.auto: screws per part pair; then look for a second contact that blocks rotation about the screw axis (or a declared join)

rules.rule: Do not carry a sustained or alternating shear load on screw friction through clearance holes or slots when a shoulder, pin or hook can carry it
rules.criterion: service load across a slotted / clearance joint <= mu (0.15) x preload x 0.65 / 2; otherwise add a positive stop (jack screw, pin)
rules.applies: belt tension anchors, motor mounts on slots, sliding mounts
rules.severity: warning: slip is what loosens screws
rules.auto: belt tension and declared loads against friction capacity of the screws in slots; credit a jack screw that touches the part

rules.rule: Nuts and tapped parts must sit on the threaded part of a partially threaded screw; the plain shank must be shorter than the grip
rules.criterion: ISO 4762 / DIN 912 thread length b: M2.5 17, M3 18, M4 20, M5 22, M6 24, M8 28 mm (Westfield); fully threaded up to M3 x 20, M4 x 25, M5 x 25, M6 x 30, M8 x 35 and partly threaded above, with lg max = l - b (Aramfix DIN 912 matrix); every nut / tapped interval must start at least lg below the head
rules.applies: long cap screws, studs made from screws
rules.severity: error: cannot be assembled as drawn
rules.auto: thread zone per screw against each threaded target's interval along the axis
rules.needs: b per size in the catalogue (already in vendor_docs CSV)
rules.correction: b and full-thread lengths recalled / from the FreeCAD CSV -> confirmed unchanged (Westfield b; Aramfix full-thread rows)

rules.rule: Use stocked lengths and sizes
rules.criterion: length in the preferred series; for lengths beyond the DIN 912 matrix rows (M3 > 30, M5 > 50) name a supplier: Lederer stocks stainless A2 / A4 M3 to 60 and M5 to 100 mm (M3 x 50, M5 x 90 included), in class 70 / 80, not 12.9
rules.where: interference STANDARD_LENGTHS_MM (used for bottoming only); ratings BOM
rules.auto: table lookup
rules.correction: M3 x 50 and M5 x 90 'outside ISO 4762's range (M3 5-30, M5 8-50)': warning -> beyond the DIN 912 matrix but stocked in A2 / A4 (Lederer): info, with the strength class to declare
rules.note: A definitive ISO 4762 length range is not verified (MISSING.txt 3).

rules.rule: Thread should show past a nut, but not far
rules.criterion: thread through a prevailing-torque (self-locking) nut: at least two threads (NASA-STD-5020B); through a plain nut: at least one pitch (recalled); not more than about 3 d unless an adjuster
rules.severity: info / warning (flush or short: nut not fully engaged)
rules.where: interference: nut counted full strength once the screw passes through
rules.auto: tip position against the nut's far face
rules.correction: 1 pitch (2 in aerospace practice, recalled) -> 2 threads for self-locking nuts (NASA-STD-5020B p.86); 1 pitch for plain nuts stays recalled

rules.rule: Threads out of the shear plane
rules.criterion: in a joint loaded in shear the plain shank, not the thread, crosses the interface
rules.applies: shear joints with loads near capacity
rules.auto: needs FST-060 data plus a load; low value for a printer

rules.rule: A screw threads into one part only
rules.criterion: 'Both parts should NEVER have threaded holes because the threads will not be in phase' (Slocum): at most one tapped part (or one nut) per screw
rules.auto: threads_into lists more than one non-nut part, or the core probe finds material of two parts

rules.rule: Every fastener on a vibrating or moving assembly has a declared locking provision
rules.criterion: every fastener on a moving or vibrating assembly has a locking feature that does not depend on preload: prevailing-torque nut (nyloc / all-metal) or thread adhesive (NASA-STD-5020B TFSR 16 states it for spaceflight; adopted here as practice). Serrated flanges and jam nuts depend on preload: accepted only where preload is assured (metal seats), never as the only feature on plastic seats
rules.applies: screws on moving bodies, motors, pulleys, bed, anything that sets an adjustment
rules.severity: warning: a printer vibrates for thousands of hours
rules.auto: per screw: body is moving or a motor is in the joint, and no locking attribute
rules.needs: add_screw(..., locking='nyloc'|'adhesive'|'serrated'|None) and nyloc / serrated catalogue parts
rules.correction: serrated flange listed as a full locking provision -> serrated / free-spinning features depend on preload (NASA): not accepted alone where the seat creeps

rules.rule: Do not specify split (helical spring) lock washers as a locking device
rules.criterion: no split lock washers in the BOM
rules.auto: BOM scan

rules.rule: Nylon-insert nuts: temperature and reuse limits
rules.criterion: nylon locking element <= about 120 degC (250 degF); replace after a few reassemblies; near the hotend or under the bed use all-metal locknuts or adhesive rated for the temperature
rules.auto: distance to el.hot_parts and the thermal estimate

rules.rule: Thread adhesives (anaerobic) attack some plastics; keep them off ABS, PC, PETG parts
rules.criterion: adhesive locking only where the screw touches metal alone; for screws through plastic use nylocs or serrated flanges
rules.auto: locking='adhesive' and a plastic in the stack

rules.rule: Tooth / star washers scratch the seat: use them for earth bonding, not as a general lock on finished or highly stressed parts
rules.criterion: star washers only at protective-earth points
rules.where: electrical: earth_point product text (ring terminals and star washer)
rules.auto: BOM scan

rules.rule: Standardise fasteners and tools
rules.criterion: target <= 2 thread sizes and <= 3 lengths per size on the main assembly; one drive type; count distinct SKUs and tools and report
rules.where: assemble / score: fastener_types, tool_changes (reported, no threshold)
rules.auto: count; suggest merges (a length only used <= 4 times with a neighbour that fits)

rules.rule: Avoid look-alike fasteners that are not interchangeable in the same area
rules.criterion: two lengths of one size differing by <= 2 mm where the shorter one is needed to avoid bottoming (e.g. M3x6 next to M3x8 into 3.5 mm-deep block threads) => warn, key or segregate
rules.applies: catalogue tapped holes with a maximum depth
rules.severity: warning: the wrong screw jams a guide block or cracks a motor end bell
rules.auto: per sub-assembly: would the next longer SKU in the BOM bottom out here?

rules.rule: Screws driven straight into printed plastic are for one-time, low-load joints
rules.criterion: no machine screw threaded directly into a printed part where the joint is structural or re-opened; use insert, captive nut or through-bolt
rules.where: interference thread_engagement (2 d in plastic); manufacture fdm.thread_wall_d_ratio
rules.auto: threads_into a plastic part

rules.rule: Heat-set inserts: hole, depth and wall
rules.criterion: straight hole to the insert maker's figure (ruthex RX-M3x5,7: 4.0 mm, wall W min 1.6; RX-M5x9,5: 6.4 mm, W 2.6); blind depth insert length + 2 pitches (SPIROL) (CNC Kitchen: about 1 mm deeper); boss 2 to 3 x insert diameter (SPIROL); install flush (subflush = jack-out)
rules.auto: insert catalogue part with hole / wall data; measure the boss
rules.correction: M3 hole 4.0 (snippet), wall >= 0.5 x insert OD (snippet), depth +1 mm -> ruthex hole and W min per size; depth +2 pitches (SPIROL)
rules.note: SOURCES DISAGREE on boss size: ruthex's minimum wall (M3: 4.6 + 2 x 1.6 = 7.8 mm boss, 1.7 x d1) vs SPIROL's optimum 2 to 3 x (9.2 to 13.8 mm). SPIROL strength data are for nylon test plastics and its own inserts; not ratings for printed PETG / ABS (MISSING.txt 7).

rules.rule: Put the insert or captive nut on the side where the load pulls it INTO the part
rules.criterion: screw tension must seat the insert / nut against plastic, not draw it out of its hole
rules.auto: insert on the far side of the clamped stack from the screw head = good; same side = pull-out

rules.rule: Captive nut pockets: closed against rotation, open for insertion, with plastic behind the nut
rules.criterion: pocket across flats = nut AF + 0.2 to 0.4 mm; >= 2 mm (or 0.6 d) of plastic between nut face and the clamped interface; nut insertable in the assembled state or retained
rules.where: interference (nut overlap), assemblability (nut has a path in)
rules.auto: measure the pocket around each nut inside a printed part

rules.rule: Say which T-nut: slide-in nuts must be in the slot before the slot end is closed; drop-in / roll-in nuts for anything added later
rules.criterion: each T-nut SKU names its type; a slide-in nut in a slot whose both ends are blocked at that assembly step is an error
rules.severity: error for trapped slide-in nuts, else info
rules.where: T-nuts are BOM lines, not geometry (AGENT.md)
rules.auto: slot ends blocked at the step where the screw is fitted (assembly order exists)

rules.rule: A part on T-nuts wants two of them (or a key in the slot); a single T-nut pivots and slides
rules.criterion: parts held to an extrusion by one T-nut screw need a second constraint; loads along the slot are carried by friction only (FST-052)
rules.auto: T-nut screws per part

rules.rule: Tapped extrusion ends: tap the core hole to depth, deburr, and back the joint with a bracket where it carries moment
rules.criterion: end tap M5 in the 2020 core hole: engagement >= 2 d if the profile is 6063-class (Bossard AlMg3 F18 row, Rm > 180, mapped); a blind butt joint on one screw also needs an anti-rotation feature
rules.where: interference thread_engagement; fea AssemblyCase lower bound
rules.auto: FST-051 on extrusion ends
rules.correction: 2 d in 6063 (recalled) -> 2 d by Bossard's soft-aluminium row (mapping derived)

rules.rule: Mind galvanic pairs where moisture can stand
rules.criterion: indoors dry: stainless or zinc-plated steel in aluminium is accepted; avoid bare carbon steel sheet against aluminium without a finish; give laser-cut mild steel a finish (paint, zinc, oil)
rules.auto: material pairs in contact + declared finish

rules.rule: An earth bond through anodised or painted metal must break the coating
rules.criterion: serrated washer or scraped seat at every protective-earth joint; anodised extrusions are not bonded to each other by their brackets unless shown
rules.severity: error if a PE path relies on anodised contact
rules.auto: PE continuity graph over metal parts with joint conductivity flags

rules.rule: Exact constraint: count what holds each body; make every redundant constraint compliant, floating or adjusted
rules.criterion: per body: bearing reaction points = 6 - DOF (Slocum 3-36); each extra one needs a declared float / flexure / adjustment, or deliberate elastic averaging
rules.where: fea.bed_support constraint / z_over_constrained; tolerance two-rail and screw-to-rail checks
rules.auto: generalise the bed-support constraint count to X and Y

rules.rule: Two parallel rails: one is the master against a reference edge, the other is set parallel to it at assembly and then locked
rules.criterion: allowable non-parallelism MGN12: 9 um (ZF / Z0), 5 um (Z1): only reachable by setting the slave rail with the carriage as gauge
rules.where: tolerance: two rails parallel; Adjustment rail_align

rules.rule: A lead screw must not also be a guide: float the nut or the far end
rules.criterion: nut radial float >= 99.7 % misalignment of screw to rails; do not fix both screw ends rigidly AND the nut

rules.rule: Screws clamp, they do not locate: use dowels, shoulders, ribs-in-slots or a tight pattern where position matters
rules.criterion: screws clamp; 'Bolts and screws DO NOT themselves take shear loads, unless you use a shoulder bolt' (Slocum); a position requirement tighter than the clearance (M3 medium 3.4 - 3.0: +/-0.2 mm) needs a locating feature or an adjustment
rules.where: tolerance: joint play of screws is simulated; adjustments credited
rules.auto: list joints whose play dominates a failed stack-up and that have no locating feature

rules.rule: Two-pin location: one round hole and one slot aimed at it
rules.criterion: a part located by two pins / tight screws: second feature is a slot along the line of centres, never two tight round holes more than a few d apart
rules.auto: needs pins as parts

rules.rule: Every adjustment has (a) a controlled way to move it, (b) a lock that does not disturb it, (c) tool access in the finished machine
rules.criterion: Adjustment declares mover (jack screw, nut pair, slot by hand), lock (screws, jam nut, adhesive) and is reachable at the assembled pose
rules.severity: warning: an adjustment that drifts or cannot be reached is not one
rules.where: Adjustment has name, kind, range only
rules.auto: Adjustment(lock=[screw names], mover=...): locks must exist, be FST-070-locked, and pass driver access in the FINAL assembly, not only at their own step

rules.rule: Allow thermal growth: one fixed point, the rest free to slide or flex
rules.criterion: alpha dT L (aluminium plate 23.6e-6 /K per mechloop/parts/vendor/cast_tooling_plate.json: 0.3 mm on 220 mm at 60 K) taken by slots / flexures; 'an exactly constrained design has no chance of deforming [...] by thermal expansion' (Slocum)
rules.where: fea ThermalCase (bow, gap); AGENT.md 'fixed at one point and free to grow at the others'
rules.auto: bed held at more than one rigid point without a declared flexure

rules.rule: Abbe: keep the working point close to the guide and the drive in line with the mass centre and friction
rules.criterion: offset nozzle-to-rail and belt-to-centre-of-mass as small as layout allows; report the arms
rules.where: twin: toolhead tilt spring from block spacing and nozzle distance; fea.bed_support screw offset
rules.auto: report arms; no threshold

rules.rule: Bearing spacing against overhang (Saint-Venant / 'golden' proportion)
rules.criterion: linear guides: spacing / width L/D > 1 (below it machines jam), 1.6 very good, 3 'awesome' (Slocum 3-7)
rules.auto: ratio from block positions and tool point
rules.correction: L/D 1 / 1.6 / 3 (snippet) -> same, from the document

rules.rule: Short, closed structural loop between tool and work
rules.criterion: human review of the path nozzle - gantry - frame - Z - bed

rules.rule: Locate both members of a critical pair from the same part / the same set-up
rules.criterion: shortest chain between two features that must align
rules.where: tolerance: chains; hints 'locate both parts from one part'

rules.rule: Fit by load direction: the ring that sees a rotating load gets the tight fit
rules.criterion: rotating inner ring under a stationary load: inner ring interference fit, outer ring loose (SKF table 1); shaft up to 17 mm under light load js5 (h5), normal load up to 10 mm js5 (SKF table 2); housing H7-class loose
rules.auto: require a declared fit for each ring
rules.correction: shaft j5-k5, housing H7 (recalled) -> js5 (h5) for an 8 mm shaft under light load (SKF)

rules.rule: A printed bearing seat is a locating pocket, not a press fit that lasts
rules.criterion: bearing in plastic: retain axially by shoulder + cover / screw / circlip; do not count on interference (creep) and expect 0.1-0.3 mm radial play in a 'sliding' printed seat
rules.auto: bearing whose seat part is plastic: BRG-020 on both sides + radial clearance drawn

rules.rule: Retain the locating bearing axially in BOTH directions, on both rings
rules.criterion: each ring of the locating bearing has a shoulder, sleeve, circlip, cover or collar on both faces; the load path for axial force in each direction is drawn
rules.severity: warning (error when a declared axial load has no path)
rules.where: AGENT.md 'axial retention of bearings' not checked
rules.auto: probe the annulus above / below each ring for an abutting part (tools/practice_audit.py does)

rules.rule: One locating bearing per shaft; the other floats
rules.criterion: exactly one bearing constrained axially both ways; the other free on one ring (thermal growth, no fight)
rules.auto: from BRG-020 results per shaft

rules.rule: Axial load on a deep-groove ball bearing stays a fraction of its static rating
rules.criterion: pure axial load <= 0.5 C0; small bearings (bore up to about 12 mm) and light series <= 0.25 C0 (SKF). 608: C0 1.37 kN -> 342 N
rules.where: ratings: guide loads against catalogue ratings ('typical')
rules.auto: axial share of the joint load per bearing
rules.note: SKF's basic ratings are not permissible service loads without life, speed, fit and lubrication checks (README).
rules.correction: 0.5 / 0.25 C0 recalled, unconfirmed -> confirmed: 608 is a 'small bearing', 0.25 C0 = 342 N

rules.rule: Axial load goes through a shoulder, collar or circlip, not through set-screw friction or a press fit
rules.criterion: axial load through a shoulder, collar, circlip or nut; a set-screwed hub in the path is a warning. Capacity of a cup-point set screw on a plain steel shaft (Rc 15 to 35 / HRB 80 to 100): M3 0.71 kN (Unbrako, 0.87 N.m) to 0.88 kN (Holo-Krome, 1.0 N.m), +/-30 %; on a thread or a soft shaft no data
rules.auto: axial path from nut to frame: joins of kind set_screw / press on it
rules.note: The capacity on a proper shaft is large against a printer's loads; the objection is the seat (thread, unhardened stainless) and creep of the hub's preload, not the number.

rules.rule: What abuts a bearing ring stays inside that ring's abutment diameters
rules.criterion: 608: parts on the shaft side abut between da min 10 mm and the inner ring's shoulder d1 about 12.15 mm (ra max 0.3); housing side up to Da max 20 mm (SKF); a pulley hub, collar (Ruland MCL-8 18 mm OD) or nut wider than d1 rubs the shields / cage: put an 8 x 12 shim washer between
rules.applies: anything seated on a bearing ring
rules.severity: warning: rubbing shield, preload on the wrong ring
rules.auto: diameter of the contact annulus between each ring face and the abutting part (practice_audit measures it)
rules.needs: abutment data in the bearing catalogue

rules.rule: Set screws bear on a flat (or dimple), two at 90 degrees, and are locked
rules.criterion: hub on a shaft by set screws: M3 cup point at 0.87 to 1.0 N.m holds 0.71 to 0.88 kN axially, torsionally that x shaft radius (8 mm shaft: 2.8 N.m, Unbrako); two screws at 90 deg (Gates stock pulleys); flat or spot on the shaft for repeatable seating; thread adhesive
rules.severity: warning: the classic printer failure (layer shift)
rules.where: v8 docstring: 'pulley set screws' not modelled
rules.auto: set_screw joins: does the shaft have a flat (catalogue attribute)?
rules.needs: shaft flat on nema17(); set screw count on gt2_pulley

rules.rule: Plastic creeps under a clamped screw: spread the load and do not rely on preload
rules.criterion: screw head / nut on printed plastic => washer AND, where preload matters, a metal sleeve (compression limiter) so the clamp load goes through metal. DERIVED sustained bearing limit for printed PETG / ABS: 5 MPa at up to 40 degC, 2.5 MPa from 40 to 60 degC, no sustained clamp above 60 degC or above HDT - 15 K. Derivation: PETG's linear viscoelastic region ends at 5.3 to 8.0 MPa (Romeijn, DMA, mean 6.5); the ABS creep study held 5 MPa to stay under 2 % strain; PETG creep compliance rises about 2.5-fold over 10 years at 23 degC; PETG's creep model is valid only to 60 degC
rules.applies: every screw through a printed part
rules.severity: warning: joints go slack over weeks, faster when warm
rules.auto: first clamped part under head / nut is plastic and no washer or sleeve part (tools/practice_audit.py does)
rules.correction: 0.3 x yield, sustained (recalled): PETG about 14, ABS about 12 MPa -> 5 MPa derived (2.5 MPa between 40 and 60 degC)
rules.note: NO VALIDATED ALLOWABLE for printed PETG / ABS was found (Bossard's VDI tables are metals only; MISSING.txt 4 and 14). The 5 MPa figure is ours, labelled derived: it keeps the plastic in the linear range so creep stays predictable; it is not a strength. Test plastics differ: pellet-extruded PETG (not Prusament), Z-ABS (not ABS-M30).

rules.rule: Keep sustained load and heat off low-temperature plastics
